headline: Debora had a fall at home on 2026-10-02 and has since declined in bathing and lower-body dressing, while her spouse and caregiver Kevin reports exhaustion and asks for respite.

items.statement: On 2026-10-02 Debora fell in the kitchen while reaching for a cabinet and was found on the floor by her spouse. She denied head strike and loss of consciousness. She had a small left forearm skin tear, and fall risk was reassessed as high.
items.verifier_note: Every detail matches the 2026-10-02 nursing note: the kitchen fall, the spouse finding her, no head strike or loss of consciousness, the small left forearm skin tear, and fall risk reassessed as high.

items.statement: PT evaluation on 2026-10-05 found a slow, unsteady gait with intermittent cane use and a Timed Up and Go of 19 seconds. PT recommends a front-wheeled walker, a home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and will see her twice weekly.
items.verifier_note: The PT evaluation note matches on gait, intermittent cane use, a TUG of 19 seconds, the walker, home safety evaluation and bathroom grab bars, and twice-weekly visits.

items.statement: On 2026-10-26 OT found Debora now needs moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing; she was independent at last review. OT recommends a tub transfer bench, a handheld shower and more home care hours for bathing.
items.verifier_note: The OT note matches: moderate assistance with bathing and lower-body dressing, independent at last review, and the three recommendations.

items.statement: On 2026-10-13 Kevin, her spouse and primary caregiver, reported exhaustion and poor sleep and worry about managing evenings alone. He requested respite, and respite options and a caregiver support group were discussed.
items.verifier_note: The social work note matches on Kevin's exhaustion, poor sleep and worry about evenings, his respite request, and the respite and support group discussion.

items.statement: On 2026-10-19 the home care aide gave hands-on help getting her out of the tub. Debora said she has been skipping showers because she fears slipping.
items.verifier_note: The home care aide note says she needed hands-on help getting out of the tub and has been skipping showers for fear of slipping.

items.statement: Sertraline 25 mg was started on 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14), and the pharmacist reconciled it on 2026-09-15. The PCP planned a recheck in 4 weeks. The notes provided show no documented recheck, and the next PCP notes (2026-09-26, 2026-10-20, 2026-10-27) say only that chronic conditions are stable.
items.verifier_note: The start date, dose, PHQ-9 of 14 and 4-week recheck plan are in the 2026-09-13 note. The pharmacist's reconciliation is in the 2026-09-15 note. The three later PCP notes say only that chronic conditions are stable, with no recheck documented.

items.statement: No flu vaccine is recorded for this season, which started 2026-08-01. The last influenza vaccine was on 2026-04-25.

checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) against the last IDT review date and note any gap in documentation before the window start.

Falls and near-falls: count and document any falls, injuries, or fall-related visits since last review; note fall-risk screening status and any fall-risk medication context (e.g., new sertraline started 2026-09-13).
ED visits and hospital admissions: list any ED visits, observation stays, or admissions in the window, with reason and discharge plan; check for follow-up appointments completed.

Medication changes in the window: sertraline 25 mg was started 2026-09-13 for depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 of 14). Verify start was documented, check for follow-up PHQ-9 timing, side effects (GI upset, sleep change, bleeding risk given concurrent clopidogrel), and prescriber follow-up. Confirm no other starts or stops in the window.

Cardiac review (ischemic heart disease, onset 2025-04): review blood pressure and heart rate trend on metoprolol succinate 100 mg, chest pain or nitroglycerin use frequency, clopidogrel and simvastatin adherence, and any cardiology follow-up due.

Respiratory review (COPD/chronic obstructive bronchitis, chronic sinusitis): review rescue albuterol use frequency, exacerbations or steroid courses, inhaler technique and adherence to fluticasone/salmeterol, oxygen saturation if recorded, and sinusitis symptoms or treatments.

Weight and BMI trend (obesity, prediabetes): compare weights across the window, note direction and magnitude of change, and review most recent glucose or HbA1c and any diabetes-prevention or nutrition referrals.
Thyroid review (idiopathic atrophic hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 0.075 mg): check whether a TSH level is due or recent, adherence, and any symptoms of fatigue, weight change, or cold intolerance.

Chronic pain and function: review pain scores, analgesic use (none listed on active medication list; confirm any OTC or PRN use), ADL and IADL status, mobility, and any change in ability to complete daily tasks.

Cognition, mood, and attendance: review the PHQ-9 result that prompted sertraline, any safety screening for mood symptoms, cognitive screening status, PACE center attendance and missed days, and social engagement. Note that breast cancer history (onset 2000) warrants checking oncology surveillance status and any new breast-related symptoms.

Caregiver situation and care-plan items due: confirm caregiver availability and strain, any change in living situation or transportation, and list care-plan items, assessments, or authorizations due before 2026-11-30. Flag that the allergy list is empty and confirm it was reconciled.
